results.title: Why Open Source GTM Agents Won't Replace Your SDR Platform | Blog | MarketBetter
results.content:
### 4. No Dialer​

Phone is still the highest-conversion outbound channel in B2B. The data on this is unambiguous: multi-channel sequences that include phone connect at 2-3x the rate of email-only sequences.

Open source GTM agents are entirely text-based. No parallel dialing. No local presence numbers. No voicemail drop. No call recording, transcription, or AI-powered coaching. No integration with your CRM that logs the call, updates the contact record, and triggers the next sequence step.

The phone gap alone is disqualifying for any serious SDR operation.

## The Real Problem: Execution Infrastructure​

Here's the deeper issue. These repos conflate intelligence with infrastructure. [...] When you add it all up, "free" open source agents often cost more than a purpose-built platform — and deliver less, because you're building the infrastructure yourself.

## The Bottom Line​

Open source GTM agents are a fascinating development. They represent the bleeding edge of what's possible when you point large language models at sales and marketing workflows. I'm genuinely excited about the innovation happening in this space.

But excitement and production readiness are different things.

If you're a developer who wants to experiment with AI-driven prospecting, these repos are a playground. If you're a revenue leader who needs to hit quota, they're a distraction. [...] ## The Uncomfortable Truth About "Free"​

One more thing worth addressing: the appeal of these repos is partly that they're free. Open source. Clone and go.

But "free" in GTM tooling is a misnomer. The costs are hidden:

 API costs. Running 92 AI agents against production LLM APIs gets expensive fast. Claude, GPT-4, Gemini — none of these are free at scale.
 Data costs. The agents need data to query. Enrichment APIs, intent data feeds, contact databases — all paid.
 Engineering time. Someone has to integrate these agents into your actual workflow. Connect them to your CRM. Build the glue code. Maintain it when APIs change.
 Opportunity cost. Every hour your team spends wiring together open source agents is an hour they're not selling.

Open agent software does not make the sales supply chain open. Contact records, enrichment, email validation, mailboxes, carrier services, model APIs, and consent data remain separately licensed, metered, and regulated.

## The AI-SDR reset: what the evidence supports

AI SDRs attracted large investments and ambitious replacement claims. 11x announced a $24 million Series A in September 2024, while TechCrunch reported from sources that its Series B was roughly $50 million at about a $350 million valuation (11x, TechCrunch). The Series B figures are reported estimates, not company-confirmed facts. [...] The useful comparison is not “Which bot replaces an SDR?” It is “Which sales infrastructure should we buy, and which workflow logic should we own?”

## What “open source AI sales agent” should mean

Use three tests:

1. Code: Is the functional product source available?
2. License: Can users run, modify, and redistribute it under a recognized open-source license?
3. Deployment: Can the buyer operate the relevant product without a vendor-only control plane?

Eigent's application repository is Apache-2.0 and supports a local/self-hosted path (Eigent repository, license). The five commercial vendors in this comparison do not publish an open-source license for their core products.
